newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: S&P takes TransAlta off creditwatch neg.
newsitem.headline: S&P takes TransAlta off creditwatch neg.

text.p: Credit ratings agency Standard and Poor's on Thursday affirmed the 'A' long-term and 'A-1' short-term credit ratings on TransAlta New Zealand Ltd.
S&P removed TransAlta from creditwatch with negative implications, where it was placed on June 19. S&P said the outlook was stable.

The creditwatch placement followed TransAlta's announcement on June 17 that it intended to acquire TransAlta Energy Corp's stakes in two North Island power stations -- Southdown in Auckland and Taranaki near Stratford -- in an all-equity transaction worth NZ$44.1 million.

S&P said that after reviewing the proposed transaction and its implications for TransAlta's credit quality going forward, it was satisfied the company's solid business position remained significantly unaltered.
The majority of futures earnings and cash flow would continue to originate from TransAlta's stable distribution network business located in Wellington.
S&P said it expected TransAlta's business environment to remain stable and for the utility to retain a strong commercial position in New Zealand's electricity market.
TransAlta New Zealand is 66 percent owned by TransAlta Energy.
